summary: Returns the value as a URL, or throws.
description: An `http`, `https` or `ftp` URL with something after the scheme and no whitespace anywhere. A bare host such as `"example.com"` is not one.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a URL.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not a URL.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireUrl("https://example.com"); // => "https://example.com"
requireUrl("http://example.com/a?b=1"); // => "http://example.com/a?b=1"
requireUrl("example.com"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireUrl("https://"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
